headline: Highest risk is medium: pdf.js can parse untrusted PDFs while the paired Spring samples add no isolation or verification, creating modest prompt-injection and cascading-error exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: pdf.js ingests PDF files and can run in browser-based tests, so attacker-controlled document content could be rendered as text the other agent might consume. spring-integration-samples has no documented isolation or provenance controls. The pair lacks a proven shared channel, so this is inferred rather than directly observed, but uncertainty should escalate to medium.
conditions: IF outputs from pdf.js are copied into spring-integration-samples inputs without sanitization
IF a shared workspace or clipboard is introduced between the agents
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces
Disable copy-paste of rendered content into prompts
Add a provenance label to all pdf.js outputs
requires-engineering: add content filtering between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents report network_egress:none, and pdf.js only lists PDF files while spring-integration-samples lists no data classes touched. There is no documented shared workspace, OAuth, or secret handling, so a leakage path is not evident. The pair appears local-only, making residual risk small.
conditions: IF a shared filesystem is mounted between the agents
IF sensitive PDFs are manually copied into spring-integration-samples outputs
mitigations: Avoid placing sensitive PDFs in shared paths

C_capability_conflict.rationale: pdf.js supports multiple instances and browser-based tests, but it has no write or network permissions documented. spring-integration-samples also shows no write, network, or OAuth scopes. With no overlapping mutable resource exposed, direct capability conflict is unlikely and limited if introduced manually.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable directory
IF an orchestrator grants shared mutable state not shown in the profiles
mitigations: Avoid shared git or database state
Run one agent at a time for edits
requires-engineering: add locking around shared resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: pdf.js can produce extracted text or rendered interpretations that spring-integration-samples could treat as input, but the second agent has no documented verification step. Because the pairwise interaction is undocumented, this is inferred from general behavior; uncertainty pushes the rating to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF spring-integration-samples consumes pdf.js output as authoritative text
IF no human or automated verification is inserted between them
mitigations: Compare extracted text against the source PDF
Limit downstream actions to drafts only

E_compliance.rationale: No compliance-sensitive data class, residency mismatch, or retention policy is documented for either agent. pdf.js touches PDF documents locally and spring-integration-samples lists no data classes or regulated handling, so no specific compliance breach pathway is evidenced.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is introduced into either agent
IF a deployment adds logging or retention not shown in the profiles
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair
